summary: This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement showing a stable US$1.3 billion valuation and an occupancy rate table (87.2% in FY 2025), alongside financial highlights including US$43.0 million income available for distribution, leasing volume trends, and adjusted net property income reported in US$'000. The reporting unit is explicitly stated as US dollars (US\$).

This page details the SGX REIT's distinctive portfolio of 13 quality freehold office buildings and business campuses across US key growth markets as of 31 December 2025, featuring a committed occupancy rate of 87.2%, net lettable area of 4.8m sf, and assets under management of US$1.3b.

This page presents the SGX REIT's Financial Highlights and Quarterly Results for the year ended 31 December, reporting gross revenue of US$'000 alongside balance sheet metrics including investment properties, total assets, and unitholders' funds. The data explicitly details quarterly gross revenue trends from 2024 to 2025, distribution per unit (DPU) figures, and key financial ratios such as interest coverage and aggregate leverage.

This page presents the Trust Structure diagram and accompanying text detailing the ownership and contractual relationships of KORE US REIT across Singapore and the United States, including information on sponsors (Keppel Ltd., KPA), the trustee, manager (Keppel Capital International), and asset management agreements with Pacific Oak Capital Advisors LLC. The reporting unit is not explicitly stated in the text, though the data is as at 31 December 2025.

This page presents unitholding breakdowns by investor type (Retail 66.8%, Institutional 19.7%, Sponsors 13.5%) and geography (Singapore 36.3%, Others 53.1%, etc.) as of 9 February 2026, alongside details on KORE's multi-channel investor engagement activities including roadshows, webinars, and the Annual General Meeting.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement by valuation, trade sector breakdown (by CRI and committed NLA), and portfolio performance by gross revenue for KORE as of 31 December 2025, reporting all figures in percentages. The main artifact is the donut chart titled "Portfolio by Valuation (%)" showing The Plaza Buildings as the largest segment at 21.7%, alongside tables detailing property valuations, tenant mix across five sectors (led by TAMI at 41.6%), and gross revenue distribution (led by The Plaza Buildings at 17.0%).

This page highlights the strategic redevelopment of 1150 Iron Point and reports that KORE leased 622,029 sf in FY 2025 with a committed portfolio occupancy of 87.2% as at 31 December 2025, detailed in the **Portfolio Committed Occupancy by NLA (%)** table which lists specific property values including Iron Point at 80.4%.

This page presents a Top-N tenants table showing Comdata, Inc. as the largest tenant with 4.0% of the portfolio by CRI and 3.9% by NLA, alongside lease expiry profiles indicating no more than 19.2% of total committed leases by CRI expire in any single year over the next five years. The reporting unit is SGD'000 (CRI) and S$ million (NLA).

This page presents the **Statement of Portfolio (property valuations)** for The Westpark REIT's US properties as at 31 December 2025, detailing latest valuations and purchase prices in **US$ million** across four locations. The table explicitly names principal tenants by portfolio and lists key metrics including net lettable area, occupancy rates, ownership interest, and acquisition dates.

This page presents a Statement of Portfolio (property valuations) for the SGX REIT as at 31 December 2025, listing five properties in Texas and Florida with their latest US$ million valuations, locations, ownership interests, acquisition dates, net lettable areas, committed occupancy rates, and tenant counts. It explicitly names principal tenants for each asset but does not contain audited financial statements, revenue/expense data, distribution highlights, or trade mix tables.
This page details the Plaza Buildings development in Bellevue, Washington, presenting a Trade Sector Breakdown by Committed NLA (%) and Top Three Tenants by CRI as of 31 December 2025.

This page presents the Bellevue Technology Center's trade sector breakdown by committed NLA as at 31 December 2025, showing TAMI (62.9%), Professional Services (33.4%), Finance and Insurance (2.2%), and Medical and Healthcare (1.5%), alongside a table of the top three tenants by CRI: TerraPower (47.1%), Regus (10.7%), and Trane U.S. (9.7%). It also details the lease expiry profile percentages for years 2026 through 'beyond' split by CRI and Committed NLA, with no audited portfolio statements, financial highlights, or reporting unit schema data present.

This page details The Westpark Portfolio in Redmond, Washington, featuring a donut chart and table for the **Trade Sector Breakdown by Committed NLA (%) as at 31 December 2025** (TAMI 46.3%, Professional Services 27.2%, Medical and Healthcare 9.5%, Finance and Insurance 0.4%, Others 16.6%) and a table listing the **Top Three Tenants by CRI (%) as at 31 December 2025** (MicroSurgical Technology 7.8%, Digital Intelligence Systems 5.1%, Wildlife Computers 4.4%). Additionally, it presents a **Lease Expiry Profile (%) as at 31 December 2025**, reporting lease expirations by year through 2031 & beyond split into two columns labeled "By CRI" and "By Committed NLA".

This page details the property profile and asset-level metrics for Great Hills Plaza, a three-storey office building in Austin, Texas, featuring a donut chart of the trade sector breakdown by committed NLA as at 31 December 2025. It explicitly presents a Top-N tenants table (Ferrovial, Regus, Pattern Bioscience) ranked by CRI, alongside a lease expiry profile showing annual percentages through 2031 & beyond.

This page features a donut chart and table detailing the Trade Sector Breakdown by Committed NLA (%) as at 31 December 2025, followed by a table listing the Top Three Tenants by CRI for the same date. The content also includes a lease expiry profile (%) by year from 2026 to 2031 & beyond, with no audited Portfolio Statement, financial statements, or manager/trustee information present.

This page details the Westmoor Center business campus in Denver, featuring a trade sector breakdown by committed NLA dominated by TAMI (86.4%), and a top-three tenants table by CRI listing BAE Systems (46.5%) and Highridge Medical (28.4%). The reporting unit is not explicitly stated, but all percentage figures are provided as of 31 December 2025.

This page presents the property profile and operational metrics for 105 Edgeview, including a Trade Sector Breakdown by Committed NLA (%) and Top Three Tenants by CRI as at 31 December 2025, alongside a Lease Expiry Profile table.

This page presents a property profile for Bridge Crossing in Nashville, Tennessee, featuring tables detailing the trade sector breakdown (100% TAMI), top three tenants by CRI (Comdata at 95.7%, Cognizant Technology at 4.3%), and lease expiry profiles as of 31 December 2025. The reporting unit is not explicitly stated with currency symbols or scale labels in the provided text.

This page presents a property profile for 1800 West Loop South, Houston, Texas, including trade sector breakdowns and top-tenant data as at 31 December 2025. The content explicitly includes the Top-N tenants/customers table (Health Care Service Corporation, Endo1 Partners, Third Coast Bank SSB) and a Trade/Tenant mix table showing committed NLA percentages across six sectors, with no audited portfolio statements or financial highlights present.

This page details the Bellaire Park property in Houston, Texas, featuring a trade sector breakdown by committed NLA as at 31 December 2025 showing Medical and Healthcare (58.4%), Professional Services (26.9%), Finance and Insurance (3.6%), and Others (11.1%), alongside a top-three tenants table by CRI listing Eyesouth Eye Care Services (10.5%), Resource Environmental Solutions (9.3%), and SCP Eye Care Services (5.1%). A lease expiry profile (%) table also presents distribution percentages through 2031 and beyond split by CRI and Committed NLA.

This page presents the One Twenty Five office complex portfolio with a trade sector breakdown by committed NLA (Finance and Insurance 19.1%, Professional Services 16.7%, Medical and Healthcare 14.6%, TAMI 5.5%, Others 44.1%) as at 31 December 2025, alongside tables detailing the top three tenants by CRI (U.S. Homeland Security 19.6%, United Capital Financial Advisor 16.9%, Bio Medical Applications of Texas 15.9%) and lease expiry profiles by CRI and Committed NLA for years 2026 through beyond.

This page presents property-specific data for Maitland Promenade I & II, featuring a trade sector breakdown by committed NLA (TAMI 52.0%, Finance and Insurance 26.9%, Professional Services 21.1%) and a top-tenant table by CRI (Spectrum Sunshine State 29.1%, AssistRx 14.8%, Burns & McDonnell 11.3%). Additionally, it displays the lease expiry profile as percentages by year through 2031 and beyond, with no audited portfolio statements, financial highlights, or reporting unit schema specified.

This page presents Iron Point's trade sector breakdown by committed net lettable area (NLA) as at 31 December 2025, identifying Professional Services as the largest segment at 41.4%, alongside a top-three tenants table by contract rental income (CRI) and a lease expiry profile chart comparing CRI and committed NLA percentages from 2026 through 2031 and beyond.

This page presents the Financial Review with a table detailing revenue, expenses, and net income for SGD'000 (US$'000), explicitly listing gross revenue of $150,165 and property expenses totaling $(69,509). The table concludes with the calculation of distribution adjustments and income available for distribution to Unitholders at $43,032.

This page presents a DPU/financial highlights section reporting US$150.2m gross revenue and US$80.7m net property income for FY 2025, accompanied by a Gross Revenue by Asset table listing performance across 13 specific assets such as The Plaza Buildings, Bellevue Technology Center, and Iron Point.

This page presents the Net Property Income Contribution by Asset table for FY 2025 (US$m) alongside narrative disclosures on Gross Revenue, Net Property Income, and Finance Expenses. The reporting unit is explicitly stated as US$m.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement (property valuations) for KORE REIT, detailing a portfolio value of US$1.3 billion as at 31 December 2025 with specific property-level valuations and a net fair value loss of US$40.5 million recognized in FY 2025. The reporting unit is explicitly stated as US$ million throughout the document.

This page presents a Debt Maturity Profile table showing the percentage of debt maturing annually from 2026 to 2030, followed by narrative details on NAV, gross borrowings, and refinancing activities for KORE. It concludes with an Interest Coverage Ratio (ICR) table reporting the ICR as 2.5 times for 2025 alongside sensitivity scenarios, while all financial figures are denominated in US dollars.

This page presents a KEY STATISTICS table detailing KORE's aggregate leverage (44.1% for 2025), weighted average all-in interest rate (4.66% p.a.), Interest Coverage Ratio (2.5 times), and weighted average term to maturity, alongside narrative disclosures on cash flows, liquidity, capital management policies, financial risk exposure, and accounting standards prepared under IFRS, MAS CIS Code, and the Trust Deed.

This page details KORE's ESG targets and commitments aligned with the UN SDGs, organized into three sustainability pillars: Environmental Stewardship (Climate Action, Waste Management, Water Management), Responsible Business (Building and Service Quality), and Corporate Governance. It presents a table outlining specific targets for FY 2025 performance metrics such as Scope 1 and 2 emissions reductions (12.5% reduction by end-2025) and waste recycling rates (21%), alongside references to pages 60–69 for further information, without providing audited portfolio statements or financial highlights in SGD'000 or S$ million.

This page presents a table detailing ESG factors, UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), targets, and FY 2025 performance metrics for Keppel FM&I's human capital management, employee health, and community engagement initiatives. Additionally, the text describes KORE's external memberships with industry associations like REITAS and SIAS, its participation in the UN Global Compact and PRI Principles, and highlights sustainability certifications including LEED Gold status for the Westmoor Center.

This page presents the Environmental Stewardship section featuring a table of Total Scope 1 and 2 GHG Emissions (tCO₂e) and GHG Intensity (tCO₂e/m²) for KORE from 2019 to 2025, alongside charts illustrating these metrics. The data reflects restated figures due to improved data availability and updated EPA emission factors, with footnotes detailing calculation methodologies including the operational control approach of the GHG Protocol and specific adjustments for biogenic emissions.

This page presents the Qualitative Physical and Transition Risk Assessment tables for KORE, detailing potential business impacts and responses to risks such as extreme precipitation, carbon pricing, and regulatory changes across short, medium, and long-term horizons. No financial statements, portfolio data, or distribution highlights are present on this page.

The page presents a table titled "TOTAL WASTE GENERATED" detailing KORE's non-hazardous waste generation and intensity from 2023 to 2025, alongside a dual-axis chart visualizing the increase in waste generated from 1,850 to 2,209 tonnes and waste intensity from 0.0041 to 0.0049 tonne/m². The content focuses on environmental stewardship metrics including transition risk quantification, green certificate costs, and waste management performance without containing any audited portfolio statements, financial income/expense tables, tenant data, or distribution highlights.

This page presents the **TOTAL WATER CONSUMPTION** table and chart, reporting consolidated water consumption of 327.3 ML and an intensity of 0.00072 ML/m² for FY2025 (SGD'000) alongside a detailed methodology note explaining the estimation technique used due to data limitations.

This page presents the GRI Content Index for KORE US REIT's sustainability reporting, covering standards from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025 and detailing disclosures across Organisational details, Activities and Workers, Governance, Strategy, Policies and Practices, Stakeholder Engagement, and Material Topics. No financial tables such as audited Portfolio Statements, Total Return statements, or distribution highlights are present on this page.

This page presents the GRI and IFRS S2 Content Index, listing disclosure requirements for people, community, employee health, and climate-related governance and strategy with corresponding page references. No schema-relevant data such as audited Portfolio Statements, financial highlights, or tenant tables are present on this page.

This page details IFRS S2 disclosure requirements for SGX REIT's climate-related scenario analysis inputs, risk management processes, and greenhouse gas metrics. It specifies that absolute gross emissions (Scope 1, 2, and 3) must be disclosed in metric tonnes of CO2 equivalent on pages 59 to 60, while scenario analysis parameters and risk assessment criteria are referenced across pages 57 to 61.

This page presents the IFRS S2 Industry-Based Guidance Metrics table for KORE US REIT, detailing energy and water management data, climate change adaptation figures, and activity metrics such as leasable floor area and occupancy rates. The reporting unit is expressed in square feet (sf) and square meters (m²), with specific portfolio details noting 13 assets across the Office Sector.

This page lists the table of contents for an SGX REIT annual report, explicitly naming the Consolidated Statement of Comprehensive Income (covering revenue, expenses, management fees, finance costs, fair-value changes, and tax) and the Consolidated Portfolio Statement (property valuations), with all financial figures reported in SGD'000 as indicated by the standard reporting unit for such statements.

This page contains the Independent Auditor's Report to the Unitholders of KORE US REIT for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, presenting an opinion that the Group's consolidated financial statements are properly drawn up in accordance with IFRS and MAS requirements. The report details a Key Audit Matter regarding the valuation of investment properties as at 31 December 2025, which held a carrying amount of US$1,325.4 million representing 95.4% of total assets, without including any audited Portfolio Statement, revenue tables, tenant mix data, or DPU/financial highlights.
This page presents the **Statements of Financial Position** for the Group and Trust as at 31 December 2025, reporting total assets of US$'000 and net asset value per unit in US$.

This page presents the Consolidated Statement of Comprehensive Income for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, reporting Group results in US$'000. It details gross revenue and property expenses to derive net property income, followed by finance costs (including manager's base fees, trustee's fee, and finance expenses), fair-value changes in derivatives and investment properties, and tax credits to arrive at a net loss attributable to Unitholders of $(4,075) thousand, along with basic and diluted earnings per unit of $(0.39) cents.

This page presents the Consolidated Distribution Statement for SGX REIT's financial year ended 31 December 2025, reporting US$'000 units. It details the income available for distribution to Unitholders at the beginning and end of the year ($43,032 and $2,611 respectively), net loss for the year, and specific distribution adjustments comprising property-related non-cash items, trustee fees, amortisation of debt costs, deferred tax, fair value changes, and others.

This page presents the Statements of Changes in Unitholders' Funds for the financial years ended 31 December 2025 and 31 December 2024, reporting unit values in US$'000. The table details a net loss for both periods resulting in retained earnings reductions to $25,233 (2025) and $29,308 (2024), while noting that distributions to unitholders were suspended from H2 2023.

The page presents the Attributable to Unitholders Statement of Total Return in SGD'000, detailing units in issue and retained earnings for the year ended 31 December 2025 alongside comparative figures for 2024. It reports a net loss of US$2,255,000 for 2025 and a net income of US$22,603,000 for 2024, with no distributions paid during either period as they were suspended from H2 2023.

This page presents the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows for SGX REIT Group for the year ended 31 December 2025, reporting net cash generated from operating activities of US$'000 76,931 and net cash used in financing activities of US$'000 20,883. The table details cash flows across operating, investing, and financing sections with values denominated in US$'000.

This page presents the **Consolidated Portfolio Statement** as at 31 December 2025, detailing fair values and asset allocations for 12 properties in US locations such as Bellevue, Austin, Denver, Houston, Dallas, Orlando, Nashville, and Sacramento. The statement reports total investment properties valued at US$'000 with a net asset balance of US$'000, though it does not include any audited portfolio statements, income statements, revenue details, tenant lists, or financial highlights.

This page contains no schema-relevant data, as it presents only accounting policy notes regarding subsidiaries, foreign currency treatment, and investment properties without including any financial tables or artifacts.

This page presents the Statement of Total Return for Trade and Other Receivables, detailing Group and Trust financial assets carried at amortised cost alongside movements in the allowance for expected credit losses. The reporting unit is US$'000.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement (property valuations) under Note 7, detailing the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position and Comprehensive Income for investment properties valued at US$'000. The table explicitly records fair value changes in investment properties and net fair value change recognised in the income statement, alongside capital expenditure capitalised, without including top-N tenants, trade mix, or distribution highlights.

This page presents the Trust's Investments in Subsidiaries, detailing the reconciliation of unquoted equity investments at cost for 2025 and 2024 in US$'000 (ending at 1,285,527 and 1,281,859 respectively) alongside a table listing eight direct and four indirect subsidiaries with their principal activities, countries of incorporation, and effective equity held percentages. The reporting unit is specified as US$'000.

This page presents a table of investments in subsidiaries detailing the names, principal activities, countries of incorporation, and effective equity held percentages for KORE entities and Keppel-KBS US REIT B1 SRL as of 31 December 2025. Additionally, it includes a Statement of Total Return (Note 9) showing trade and other payables alongside loans, borrowings, and preferred units, with all financial figures reported in US$'000.

This page presents the Loans and Borrowings table detailing current and non-current USD term loans, revolving credit facilities, unamortised transaction costs, and total borrowings for SGX REIT Group and Trust as of 31 December 2025 (reported in US$'000), alongside loan covenants requiring aggregate leverage below 50% and an interest coverage ratio of at least 1.5 times.

This page presents financial data for Preferred Units and Deferred Tax Liabilities, specifically detailing the issuance and redemption of preferred units classified as financial liabilities under IFRS 9 and the movements in deferred tax liabilities arising from investment properties. All monetary figures are reported in US$'000 across Group-level tables covering periods ending at 31 December 2024 and 2025.

This page of the SGX REIT annual report for the year ended 31 December 2025 presents Notes 13 and 14, detailing Units in Issue and Net Asset Value per Unit with data reported in US$'000. The primary artifact is a table showing that both the Group and Trust held 1,044,450 units valued at $687,002 (US$'000) as at 1 January/31 December 2025, alongside a second table confirming the Net Asset Value per Unit is based on net assets of $712,235 (US$'000) and total units issued of 1,044,450 ('000).

This page presents four tables detailing the SGX REIT Group's financial performance in US$'000, specifically covering Gross Revenue (Rental income, Recoveries income, Other operating income), Property Expenses (Utilities, Repair and maintenance, Property management fees, Property taxes, Other property expenses), Finance Expenses (Effective interest expense on loans and borrowings, Dividends on preferred units, Commitment fees), and Other Trust Expenses (Audit fees, Non-audit fees, Internal audit fees, Valuation fees, Other expenses). The reporting unit is explicitly stated as US$'000.

This page presents the Tax Credit and Earnings Per Unit (EPS) notes for the SGX REIT group, detailing a US$'000 reconciliation of tax credit components including income tax and deferred tax movements, alongside basic and diluted EPS calculations based on 1,044,450,000 weighted average units. The reporting unit is explicitly stated as GROUP with figures in US\$'000.

This page presents the SGX'000 audited table of significant related party transactions for the Manager's base fees and Trustee fees, alongside SGX'000 financial ratios including expenses to weighted average net assets and portfolio turnover rate. It also details the Group's financial risk management objectives and policies covering tax, operational, market, interest rate, credit, liquidity, capital management, and climate change risks.

This page details the Group's credit risk assessment for trade and other receivables, confirming insignificant inherent risk as of the reporting date, followed by a Liquidity Risk table presenting contractual maturities of financial liabilities (including trade payables, loans, security deposits, preferred units, and interest rate swaps) in US$'000 for both 2025 and 2024.

This page of the SGX REIT annual report for the financial year ended 31 December 2025 presents a table in US$'000 detailing the contractual maturities of financial liabilities (carrying amounts and cash flows within 1 year, after 1-5 years, and after 5 years) for both 2025 and 2024, followed by text describing capital management risk objectives including yield monitoring.

This page details the Group's aggregate leverage ratio of 44.1% as at 31 December 2025, confirming compliance with the 50% limit defined in the Property Funds Appendix, alongside a discussion on climate change risk management and TCFD categories. The reporting unit is SGD'000 based on the context of an SGX REIT annual report, though no specific audited Portfolio Statement, total return table, or financial highlights are present.

This page presents the "Fair Value of Assets and Liabilities" table for both the Group and Trust, detailing financial assets (interest rate swaps) and non-financial assets (commercial investment properties) measured at fair value using Level 2 and Level 3 inputs in US$'000. The reporting unit is explicitly stated as US$'000.

This page presents a Level 1 and Level 2 fair value measurement table for the GROUP and TRUST, detailing financial assets (interest rate swaps) at US$'000 and investment properties valued at Level 3 in US$'000. The accompanying text describes valuation techniques for derivatives using market interest rates and independent professional valuations for investment properties based on open market values.

This page of the SGX REIT annual report for the financial year ended 31 December 2025 contains descriptive notes on Level 3 fair value measurement techniques (direct comparison, capitalisation, and discounted cash flow) and unobservable inputs for investment properties valued at US$1,325.4 million as at that date, but includes no audited Portfolio Statement, Top-N tenants table, trade/tenant mix, DPU highlights, or other schema-relevant data.

This page presents the Fair Value of Financial Instruments, Operating Lease Commitments (as lessor) with a future minimum payments receivable table denominated in US$'000, Capital Commitments for investment properties also in US$'000, and Subsequent Events including a term loan facility and a distribution announcement. No audited Portfolio Statement, Profit or Loss, Top-N tenants, DPU/financial highlights, or manager/trustee/sponsor details are present on this page.

This page contains the ANNUAL REMUNERATION REPORT and a table detailing the remuneration policy for Directors, listing specific annual fees in S$ per annum for Chairman, Lead Independent Director, and Member roles across the Main Board and three committees.

This page presents a table listing the Directors seeking Unitholder endorsement for the 2026 annual general meeting, specifically detailing Mr Lawrence D. Sperling and Mr Kenneth Tan Jhu Hwa with their appointment dates, ages, roles (including Lead Independent Director and Independent Director), professional qualifications, recent work experience, shareholding interests in KORE US REIT, and confirmation of no conflicts of interest or bankruptcy history.

This page contains a Summary of Disclosures regarding the 2018 Code under Rule 710 of the SGX Listing Manual, presented as two tables mapping corporate governance principles to specific page references within the report. The primary artifacts are disclosure index tables covering Board Matters, Remuneration Matters, Accountability and Audit, Shareholder Rights, and Stakeholder Management, with no audited Portfolio Statement, financial highlights, or tenant data present.

This page presents the table of Interested Person Transactions for FY 2025, listing aggregate values in US$'000 for fees paid to KORE US REIT Management Pte. Ltd. (Manager) and Perpetual (Asia) Ltd (Trustee), alongside a note directing readers to Note 21 in the financial statements for significant related party transactions.

This page presents Unit Price Performance for KORE, featuring a monthly trading table and summary showing US$0.235 closing price on 31 December 2025, total trading volume of 270.5 million Units, and a 14.6% Total Unitholder return. The content also includes comparative data against indices (STI, FTSE ST RE Index, FTSE ST REIT Index) and highest/lowest/average prices for the period, but does not contain any audited Portfolio Statement, financial statements, gross revenue notes, tenant mix, DPU highlights, or manager/trustee information.

This page presents the unitholdings statistics for KORE US REIT as of 27 February 2026, featuring a table detailing the distribution of holdings across 5,974 unitholders and a separate table listing the twenty largest unitholders. The reporting unit is expressed in Units with no specific currency scale (SGD'000 or S$ million) applied to the holding data.

The page presents the Manager's Directors' Unitholdings and Substantial Unitholders tables for KORE US REIT as of 21 January 2026 and 27 February 2026, respectively, detailing direct and deemed unit interests held by named directors and substantial holders with corresponding percentages. It also confirms that approximately 77.52% of issued units are held by the public and notes there are no treasury units held by the REIT or its Manager.

This page contains the Proxy Form for KORE US REIT's Annual General Meeting (AGM) held on 16 April 2026, which includes a voting table for Ordinary Business resolutions such as adopting Audited Financial Statements for the year ended 31 December 2025 and re-appointing Ernst & Young LLP as Auditor, alongside Special Business resolutions to authorise Unit issuance and approve the renewal of the Unit Buy-Back Mandate. The document specifies that no unitholders may participate virtually and provides instructions for appointing proxies to vote or abstain at the physical event at Marina Bay Sands Expo and Convention Centre.
